- If sentiment is positive (≥0.33) and forecast is trending up, reduce upward bias by 5–10% to avoid overestimating price rise.
- If sentiment is neutral or negative (≤0.20) and forecast is trending down, avoid excessive downward bias; consider slight upward adjustment to prevent premature sell-off.
- When price has recently spiked (last 3–5 days > 72.0), model tends to overreact — cap forecast peak at +10% above true peak to avoid overshoot.
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 71.0), model often overcorrects — reduce forecast slope downward by 2–5% to align with reversion.
- For 30-day horizon, if last 18 days show low volatility (<±1.5% daily), forecast should not deviate more than ±2.0% from recent mean; otherwise, apply smoothing filter.
- If sentiment history shows no recent change (all 0.00), forecast should be anchored to recent 10-day average, not extrapolated from 30-day trend.
